card.title: Act as If It’s True
card.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Reserve two chairs for her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use mine. I won't make either of her eat standing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requests two chairs for one sister and future self; A3 sacrifices A's chair and A5 labels tomorrow for useful temporal identification.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 only one seat prompts A3 offering A's; B4 placing it beside the other prompts A5 a distinguishing place card.

relationship.evidence: B2 has planned ordinary seating and B4 adapts it cooperatively, allowing A's request to become more practical.

heightening.evidence: B4 creates two adjacent seats; A5 adds an identifier tied to the actual advantage of the future guest.

specificity.evidence: A1 dinner and future self clearly establish the impossible premise; A3 spare seat makes the logistical cost concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 asking how tonight went earns its wit from the specific future-self seat B4 has supplied.
